gpu-clock-tradeoff.title: GPU core clock — gain vs cost
gpu-clock-tradeoff.subtitle: More clock means more FPS, but the curve flattens once the CPU limits it, while heat and power keep climbing.

undervolt-tradeoff.title: Undervolt — cooler and quieter, until it crashes
undervolt-tradeoff.subtitle: Lower voltage cuts heat and power, but the stability margin shrinks with every step down.
undervolt-tradeoff.note: Below 700 mV the GPU locks itself to 1500 MHz.

memory-tradeoff.title: GDDR6 memory tuning — tiny gain, brick cliff
memory-tradeoff.subtitle: Clock and timings add very little FPS, and one bad value can permanently brick the board.
memory-tradeoff.note: 1950 MHz is where boards came back bricked.

cu40-tradeoff.title: 40-CU unlock — big compute gain, tiny gaming gain
cu40-tradeoff.subtitle: More CUs help compute a lot and games barely, because games are CPU-bound; the last CUs are a lottery.

band.label: 38 CU is the typical stable maximum

cu40-tradeoff.note: 40 CU is a lottery: artifacts and crashes; needs >300 W (J2000) and an AIO.

idle-power-tradeoff.title: Idle power — you can cut the GPU, not the total
idle-power-tradeoff.subtitle: Governor and undervolt drop the GPU, but CPU and GDDR6 stay fixed, so wall draw barely moves until suspend.
idle-power-tradeoff.note: High-leakage batches floor around 70–80 W; suspend reaches ~10 W.
